gloss: wind, breath, spirit; scent, smell; room, relief
summary: The root is moving air. רוּחַ is the wind, the breath of the mouth, and the breath of life that God gives to man and beast alike and takes back at death (Gen 7:22; Ecc 3:19; 12:7); from breath it is the inner man, his mind, temper and courage (Pro 16:32; Isa 66:2), and the spirit of Yahweh is his own breath and power, by which he creates, is present everywhere, gives strength and prophecy, and which he pours out (Gen 1:2; Psa 33:6; 139:7; Mic 3:8; Joel 3:1). רֵיחַ is the scent the air carries and the verb is to smell it: the offerings of Lev 23 are “a scent of soothing to Yahweh” (Lev 23:13, 18), and to smell an offering is to accept it. רָוַח, רֶוַח and רְוָחָה are room to breathe: space between, and relief when trouble lifts (Gen 32:17; 1Sa 16:23; Est 4:14). Arabic rūḥ “spirit”, rīḥ “wind”, rāʾiḥa “smell”, rāḥa “rest, ease” and rawaḥ “width”, and Ugaritic rḥ “wind, spirit”, have the same spread.

words.summary: Mostly feminine, sometimes masculine. One word for wind, breath and spirit: the senses run into one another, as in Ezk 37:9, where the prophet calls the breath from the four winds into the slain.

senses.definition: Air in motion: the wind that Yahweh brings out of his storehouses and sends to dry the waters, drive the locusts, bring the quails and break ships; it blows where it will and cannot be held.

evidence.note: God made a wind pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
Yahweh drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night.
A wind went out from Yahweh and brought quails from the sea.
The wind goes to the south and turns to the north, round and round, and returns on its circuits.
An east wind brought the locusts; a west wind took them away (Exo 10:19).
A great and strong wind tore the mountains, but Yahweh was not in the wind.
He brings the wind out of his storehouses.
Stormy wind fulfilling his word.
The wicked are like chaff that the wind drives away.
Yahweh hurled a great wind on the sea.
He who watches the wind will not sow.
You do not know the way of the רוּחַ, nor how the bones grow in the womb.
Yahweh God walking in the garden לְרוּחַ הַיּוֹם, at the breeze of the day.
He makes his messengers winds (רוּחוֹת), his ministers a flaming fire; Heb 1:7 quotes it.
The wind (πνεῦμα; the Peshitta רוּחָא) blows where it wills; so is everyone born of the spirit.

senses.definition: The four winds are the four directions, and a רוּחַ is one side of a building or a land.

evidence.note: The gatekeepers were on the four winds: east, west, north and south.
He measured the east side (רוּחַ הַקָּדִים), the north side, the south side and the west side; he measured it on the four winds.
Four winds from the four ends of the heavens, scattering Elam toward all those winds.
Four horns toward the four winds of the heavens.
His kingdom divided toward the four winds of the heavens.
I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heavens.
I will scatter all your remnant to every wind.
Four angels holding the four winds of the earth.

senses.definition: What has no substance: wind as the image of words, hopes and labour that come to nothing.

evidence.note: Their works are nothing; their molten images are wind and emptiness.
The prophets will become wind; the word is not in them.
Is there an end to words of wind?
All is vapour and striving after wind.
Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the east wind.
He who troubles his own house will inherit wind.
A man walking in wind and falsehood.
They sow wind and reap the whirlwind.

senses.definition: The air breathed out of the mouth or nostrils, and the power of what is said with it.

evidence.note: My breath is strange to my wife.
He will not let me get my breath.
The idols have ears and do not hear; there is no breath in their mouths.
His molten image is falsehood; there is no breath in them.
There is no breath at all in the overlaid idol.
At the breath of your nostrils the waters were heaped up.
By the breath of God they perish; by the רוּחַ of his anger they are consumed.
With the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked; 2Th 2:8 takes it up of Christ.
By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, by the breath of his mouth all their host.
The wild asses pant for air like jackals.
The breath of our nostrils, Yahweh's anointed, was taken in their pits.

senses.definition: The breath that makes flesh alive, shared by man and beast; God gives it and takes it back, and without it the body returns to dust. Its return in a fainting man is his reviving.

evidence.note: All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life (נִשְׁמַת־רוּחַ חַיִּים) died.
To destroy all flesh in which is the spirit of life.
Man and beast all have one breath; man has no advantage over the beast; all go to one place.
You take away their breath, they die and return to their dust; you send forth your spirit, they are created.
The dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
Two of all flesh in which is the spirit of life came into the ark.
His breath goes out, he returns to his earth; in that day his thoughts perish.
If he gathers to himself his spirit and his breath, all flesh perishes together.
In his hand is the soul of every living thing and the breath of all mankind.
He gives breath (נְשָׁמָה) to the people on the earth and spirit to those who walk in it.
He forms the spirit of man within him.
He remembered that they were flesh, a breath that passes and does not return.
Remember that my life is a breath.
No man has power over the spirit, to retain the spirit, nor power over the day of death.
Into your hand I commit my spirit; Jesus' words on the cross (Luk 23:46).
Breath from the four winds enters the slain and they live and stand up.
Samson drank, his spirit returned, and he revived.
The Egyptian ate, and his spirit came back to him.
The spirit of Jacob their father revived.

senses.definition: The inner man as he thinks, feels and wills: his mind and what comes into it, his temper (patient or hasty, lowly or proud), his courage, and the disposition that moves him.

evidence.note: He who rules his spirit is better than he who takes a city; set beside “slow to anger”.
The patient (long) of spirit is better than the proud (high) of spirit; do not be quick in your spirit to be angry.
What comes up on your spirit (mind) shall never be.
Our heart melted, and no spirit remained in anyone because of you: courage.
The humble and contrite of spirit who trembles at my word.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and crushed heart.
With the contrite and lowly of spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly.
In the morning his spirit was troubled.
Why is your spirit so sullen?
Caleb, because another spirit was with him and he followed me fully.
Everyone whose spirit made him willing brought Yahweh's offering.
Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Cyrus.
Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, of Joshua and of all the remnant.
A spirit of jealousy comes on him.
A spirit of whoredom has led them astray.
Their spirit (anger) toward him abated.
A haughty spirit before a fall.
In whose spirit there is no deceit.
Renew a steadfast spirit within me.
A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you.
The spirit of my belly presses me: what fills him and must be spoken.

senses.definition: God's own breath and power: by it he creates and gives life, it is present wherever he is, and it comes on men to give them strength, skill, wisdom and prophecy. It is set beside his power and his presence, set against flesh, taken from one man and put on others, and poured out like water.

evidence.note: The spirit of God hovering over the face of the waters.
Where shall I go from your spirit, or flee from your face (presence)?
I am full of power, of the spirit of Yahweh, of judgment and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression.
The Egyptians are men and not God, their horses flesh and not spirit.
I will take of the spirit that is on you and put it on them.
When the spirit rested on the seventy they prophesied; would that Yahweh would put his spirit on all his people.
The spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
By his spirit he made the heavens fair.
You send forth your spirit, they are created, and you renew the face of the ground.
I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all workmanship.
The spirit of Yahweh rushed on him and he tore the lion.
The spirit of Yahweh was on Othniel and he judged Israel.
The spirit of Yahweh will rush on you, you will prophesy and be turned into another man.
Samuel anointed David, and the spirit of Yahweh rushed on him from that day.
The spirit of Yahweh spoke by me; his word was on my tongue.
You testified against them by your spirit through your prophets.
The words Yahweh of hosts sent by his spirit through the former prophets.
Let a double portion of your spirit be on me; the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.
The spirit of Yahweh will carry you I know not where.
The spirit lifted me up and took me away.
Who has measured the spirit of Yahweh, or as his counsellor taught him? Paul quotes it (Rom 11:34; 1Co 2:16).
Do not take your holy spirit from me.
They rebelled and grieved his holy spirit; he who put his holy spirit in their midst.
The spirit of Yahweh will rest on the shoot of Jesse, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and might.
I have put my spirit on my servant; quoted of Jesus in Mat 12:18.
The spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me; Jesus reads it as fulfilled in himself (Luk 4:18–21).
Until the spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field.
I will pour water on the thirsty, I will pour my spirit on your seed.
I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; Peter: “this is that” (Act 2:16–18).
I have poured out my spirit on the house of Israel.
I will pour on the house of David a spirit of grace and supplication; they will look on me whom they pierced.
Not by might nor by power, but by my spirit.
My spirit will not remain in man forever, for he is flesh.
I will put my spirit in you and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land.

senses.definition: A disposition or impulse that Yahweh sends on a man or a people, named by what it does: an evil spirit that troubles, a spirit of falsehood in the prophets' mouths, of confusion, of deep sleep, of enmity. Scripture says each comes from Yahweh.

evidence.note: The spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from Yahweh terrified him.
God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and they dealt treacherously: the spirit is the enmity.
Yahweh has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these your prophets.
I will put a spirit in him, he will hear a rumour and return to his land.
When David played, Saul was relieved (וְרָוַח) and the evil spirit departed from him.
An evil spirit from God rushed on Saul and he raved in the house.
In Micaiah's vision the spirit stands before Yahweh and goes out to be a spirit of falsehood in the prophets' mouths.
Yahweh has mixed a spirit of confusion within Egypt.
Yahweh has poured on you a spirit of deep sleep; Paul quotes it (Rom 11:8).
I will remove the prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

evidence.locator: Gen.1.2, רוּחַ → πνεῦμα; Psa.31.6, Isa.61.1, Jol.3.1 and Ecc.12.7 the same; πνεῦμα renders רוּחַ ×261

evidence.note: Jesus reads Isa 61:1: “the πνεῦμα of the Lord is on me”.
Peter quotes Joel 3:1–2: “I will pour out of my πνεῦμα on all flesh”.
“Into your hands I commit my πνεῦμα” (Psa 31:6).
“Who makes his messengers πνεύματα” (Psa 104:4).
“I will put my πνεῦμα on him” (Isa 42:1).
The lawless one whom the Lord will consume with the πνεῦμα of his mouth (Isa 11:4).
“God gave them a πνεῦμα of stupor” (Isa 29:10).
The πνεῦμα blows where it wills: wind and spirit in one word, as רוּחַ.
Stephen: “Lord Jesus, receive my πνεῦμα”.

evidence.locator: Exo.10.13, רוּחַ → ἄνεμος; Exo.14.21 and 1Ch.9.24 the same; ἄνεμος renders רוּחַ ×45

evidence.note: Four angels holding the four ἄνεμοι of the earth, as the four winds of Dan 7:2; 8:8; Zec 6:5.
He rebuked the ἄνεμοι and the sea.

evidence.locator: Gen.7.22, רוּחַ → πνοή; Pro.1.23 and Ezk.13.13 the same; πνοή renders רוּחַ ×3

evidence.note: He gives to all life and πνοή.
A sound as of a violent rushing πνοή.
“Who has known the νοῦς of the Lord, or who has been his counsellor?”: Isa 40:13.
The same quotation: “but we have the νοῦς of Christ”.

parallels.note: “Breath”, set beside it of the life God gives and takes back.

evidence.note: Joined: נִשְׁמַת־רוּחַ חַיִּים.

parallels.note: “Heart”, beside it of the inner man.
“Soul”, beside it of the self in distress or longing.
His “face”, presence: nowhere is out of reach of either.

opposites.note: “Flesh”: what is weak and passing against the spirit of God.

phrases.gloss: your holy spirit (his holy spirit, רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ)
an evil spirit (from Yahweh, from God)
long of spirit: patient (against גְּבַהּ־רוּחַ, proud)
short of spirit: hasty; (קֹצֶר רוּחַ) anguish

words.summary: The smell the air carries from a thing. Most of its uses are the offerings’ רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ, “a scent of soothing” to Yahweh, among them the feast offerings of Lev 23:13 and 18.

senses.definition: The smell of a thing, pleasant or foul: of clothes, a field, oils, flowers, water, wine, fire.

evidence.note: He smelled the smell of his clothes: “the smell of my son is like the smell of a field Yahweh has blessed”.
For scent your oils are good.
At the scent of water the stump will bud.
The vines in blossom give their scent.
The smell of your oils; the smell of your garments like the smell of Lebanon.
The smell of your breath like apples.
The mandrakes give their scent.
My nard gave its scent.
His scent like Lebanon.
Moab, wine left on its lees: his taste remains in him and his scent is not changed.

senses.definition: How one is regarded, said as a smell: to make someone's scent stink is to make him hateful.

evidence.note: You have made our scent stink in the eyes of Pharaoh and his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us.

senses.definition: The smell of an offering burnt on the altar, which Yahweh smells and accepts: “a scent of soothing”. He refuses it from a rebellious people and from idols' altars, and promises to accept regathered Israel itself as such a scent.

evidence.note: Yahweh smelled the scent of soothing and said he would not again curse the ground.
A burnt offering, a fire offering, a scent of soothing to Yahweh.
I will not smell the scent of your soothing.
The grain offering of the sheaf day, a fire offering to Yahweh, a scent of soothing.
The burnt offerings of the day of firstfruits, a scent of soothing to Yahweh.
The ram of the priests' ordination.
The memorial portion of the grain offering.
The peace offering.
Even the fat of the sin offering.
Vows, freewill offerings and the offerings of the appointed times.
My bread for my fire offerings, a scent of my soothing, at its appointed time.
Where they offered a scent of soothing to all their idols.
My bread, fine flour, oil and honey set before the idols as a scent of soothing.
With a scent of soothing I will accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples.
Christ gave himself an offering and sacrifice to God for a scent of sweet smell (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας, the Septuagint's words for רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ; the Peshitta רֵיחָא).
The Philippians' gift, a scent of sweet smell, an acceptable sacrifice.

evidence.locator: Gen.8.21, רֵיחַ → ὀσμήν; Lev.1.9 and Lev.23.18 the same; ὀσμή renders רֵיחַ ×45

evidence.note: Christ's self-offering εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, the Septuagint's phrase for רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ.
ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, of a gift sent to Paul.
The ὀσμή of his knowledge; to some an ὀσμή of death to death, to others of life to life.
The house was filled with the ὀσμή of the ointment.

phrases.gloss: a scent of soothing (of an offering)

words.summary: Daniel's Aramaic, used as the Hebrew: the winds of heaven, a man's spirit, and in Nebuchadnezzar's and Belshazzar's words “the spirit of the holy gods” in Daniel.

senses.definition: The wind, and the four winds of heaven.

evidence.note: The wind carried them away, and no place was found for them.
The four winds of the heavens stirred up the great sea.

senses.definition: A man's inner self: his troubled, hardened or excellent spirit.

evidence.note: My spirit was distressed within its sheath (body), and the visions of my head alarmed me.
When his heart was lifted up and his spirit hardened to act proudly.
An excellent spirit was in him.
An excellent spirit, knowledge and understanding.

senses.definition: The spirit by which Daniel interprets, which the kings call “the spirit of the holy gods”.

evidence.note: In whom is the spirit of the holy gods; no secret is too hard for you.
The queen of Belshazzar: a man in whom is the spirit of the holy gods.

words.summary: Formed from רֵיחַ and found only in the hiphil: to smell, and of God, to smell an offering, that is, to accept it.

senses.definition: Perceive a smell, as the nose does; idols, having noses, cannot.

evidence.note: He kissed him and smelled the smell of his clothes.
A nose they have, and they do not smell.
Gods of wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.
Whoever makes incense like it, to smell it, shall be cut off.
The horse smells the battle from afar.
The cord snapped as a strand of tow snaps when it smells fire: when fire touches it.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, to smell an offering's scent, and so to accept it and the one who brings it; not to smell is to refuse.

evidence.note: Yahweh smelled the scent of soothing, and said in his heart he would not curse the ground again.
I will not smell the scent of your soothing.
I hate, I reject your feasts, and I will not smell (take delight in) your solemn assemblies.
If Yahweh has stirred you up against me, let him smell an offering.

senses.definition: Once, of the shoot of Jesse: his smelling is in the fear of Yahweh, set against judging by what his eyes see and his ears hear. He takes in and judges by the fear of Yahweh as by a sense.

evidence.note: וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת יְהוָה: “and his smelling is in the fear of Yahweh; not by the sight of his eyes shall he judge”.

words.summary: Daniel's Aramaic for smell, once: the smell of fire had not passed onto the three men.

senses.definition: The smell a thing leaves on what it touches.

evidence.note: The fire had no power over their bodies, the hair of their heads was not singed, and the smell of fire had not passed on them.

words.summary: To have room, to breathe again: relief when a weight on the spirit lifts, and of rooms, airy and wide.

senses.definition: Of a man oppressed in spirit: to have room again, to breathe freely, when what pressed on him goes.

evidence.note: When David played, Saul was relieved (וְרָוַח לְשָׁאוּל) and was well, and the evil spirit (רוּחַ) departed from him.
The spirit (רוּחַ) within me presses me; my belly is like wine with no vent; I will speak that I may be relieved (וְיִרְוַח לִי).

senses.definition: The participle: made wide, roomy, of upper rooms.

evidence.note: “I will build myself a house of great measure and spacious (מְרֻוָּחִים) upper rooms”, with windows cut out: the king who builds by unrighteousness.
Onesiphorus often refreshed (ἀνέψυξεν) Paul.

words.summary: Room between things, and room to breathe out of trouble. Only two uses, each fixed by its context.

senses.definition: A gap left between things.

evidence.note: Jacob tells his servants to put a space between drove and drove.

senses.definition: Room out of distress: relief beside deliverance.

evidence.note: If you keep silent, relief and deliverance (רֶוַח וְהַצָּלָה) will arise for the Jews from another place.

evidence.locator: Gen.32.17, וְרֶוַח → διάστημα (once); Est.4.14 has βοήθεια

evidence.note: An interval (διάστημα) of about three hours.

words.summary: A breathing space from affliction. Two uses.

senses.definition: Relief when affliction stops: the frogs gone, or the sufferer's breath and cry heard.

evidence.note: When Pharaoh saw that there was respite (הָרְוָחָה), he hardened his heart.
You heard my voice; do not hide your ear at my relief (לְרַוְחָתִי), at my cry: perhaps “at my breathing”, the gasping of the one in the pit.
Times of refreshing (ἀναψύξεως) from the presence of the Lord.

words.summary: The Peshitta's word wherever the Greek has πνεῦμα and often ἄνεμος, so that, as in Hebrew, wind, breath and spirit are one word in Jesus' own speech to Nicodemus.

senses.definition: The wind on the sea and the wind that blows where it wills.

evidence.note: The רוּחָא blows where it wills; so is everyone born of the רוּחָא.
He rebuked the wind and the sea.
A sound from heaven as of a violent wind.

senses.definition: The life a man yields up at death and commits to God.

evidence.note: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit (Psa 31:6).
Jesus cried with a loud voice and yielded up his spirit.
Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

senses.definition: God's spirit: given, poured out, received.

evidence.note: I will pour out of my spirit on all flesh (Joel 3:1).
The spirit of the Lord is on me (Isa 61:1).
God is spirit.
He breathed on them and said, Receive holy spirit.
Holy spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.
The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
Who makes his messengers spirits (Psa 104:4).

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for ὀσμή, including the offering's “scent of sweet smell” said of Christ.

senses.definition: A smell; above all the scent of a sacrifice accepted by God.

evidence.note: He gave himself for us an offering and sacrifice to God for a sweet smell.
The house was filled with the smell of the ointment.

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb for being opened wide and for giving relief, as Hebrew רָוַח.

senses.definition: Of the heart, opened wide toward others.

evidence.note: Our heart is enlarged (רְוִיחַ; SEDRA files the form under the verb “smell”).

senses.definition: Make room for others in oneself.

evidence.note: Be enlarged, you too, toward me.

senses.definition: Give relief to those in distress.

evidence.note: If she has relieved the afflicted.

words.summary: Once in the New Testament, for ἄνεσις.

senses.definition: Ease from a burden.

evidence.note: Not that others should have relief and you distress.

words.summary: Once in the New Testament, of the broad way.

senses.definition: Having much room.

evidence.note: Wide is the gate and broad the way that leads to destruction.

cognates.gloss: soul, spirit, the vital principle; the breath a man breathes
cognates.note: Lane's sources give it as “the vital principle” and “the breath which a man breathes, and which pervades the whole body: after its exit, he ceases to breathe”, which Lane takes to be the original idea. This answers to רוּחַ as the breath of life. Arabic ḥ (ح), not ḫ (خ), stands behind ח, as in every Arabic word of the root.

evidence.note: “A gentle wind; a breeze … breath; like رُوحٌ: said to be the primary signification”.

cognates.gloss: wind; (verb, of a day) be windy
cognates.note: Lane: rīḥ is “originally rīwḥ”, the air “made to … run its course between heaven and earth, or the breath of the air”; plural arwāḥ. The verb rāḥa is of a day that is windy, of a house “entered by the wind”, of trees that “felt the wind”. Another sense of rāḥa, rawāḥ, is going in the evening or afternoon, which may bear on Gen 3:8 לְרוּחַ הַיּוֹם.

evidence.note: “The evening; or the afternoon”.

cognates.gloss: smell, odour; (form IV) he breathed; it gave off a smell
cognates.note: Lane: rāʾiḥa and rīḥ both mean “odour, scent, or smell … whether sweet or stinking”, “a sweet odour which one perceives in the breath of the wind”; form IV ʾarāḥa “he breathed”, and of meat or water “it emitted an odour”. Breath, wind and smell are one Arabic root, as רוּחַ, רֵיחַ and the hiphil הֵרִיחַ are one Hebrew root.

cognates.gloss: rest, ease, cessation of trouble; (form X) rest, be relieved
cognates.note: Lane: rāḥa is “rest, repose, or ease; contr. of taʿab [toil] … cessation of trouble”, and rawḥ the same, “the experiencing relief from grief”. Lane's sources explain rīḥ “wind” as so called “because it generally brings rawḥ and rāḥa”. This answers to רָוַח “be relieved”, רֶוַח and רְוָחָה “relief, respite”.

evidence.note: The etymology of rīḥ from rawḥ and rāḥa.

cognates.note: Lane: “width, wideness, or ampleness”, and in particular wideness between the legs or feet. This answers to רֶוַח “space” and the pual מְרֻוָּחִים “spacious”.

Segert vocalises /rūḥ-/ and cites KTU 1.18 IV 24–25, of Aqhat's death: “may his soul (npš) go out like wind (km rḥ)”, breath and soul beside each other as רוּחַ and נֶפֶשׁ are. Ugaritic keeps ḥ (𐎈) apart from ḫ (𐎃); the word has ḥ.

evidence.note: “rḥ: rūḥ ‘wind, spirit, breath’”, with the Ethiopic words for fanning and a fan.

evidence.locator: SEM000375 rwḥ [wind] N: UGC003619 rḥ [wind] N

cognates.note: Krahmalkov's RḤ II, n.f., which he sets beside Hebrew rûaḥ: in Punic curses the goddess or god “shall adjudge the intent (rḥ) of that person” who disturbs the stone (KAI 79.6–11; CIS i 5510; CIS i 5632). The inner man as he wills, as רוּחַ is the spirit of man; no use of rḥ for wind or breath is given.

cognates.gloss: (yiphil) provide rest and comfort, make welcome
cognates.note: Krahmalkov's R-Ḥ I, comparing Arabic rāḥa: CIS i 5510.6–7, whoever calls on Milqart “they shall … make him welcome (lyrḥy) in this city”. Giving ease answers to רָוַח “be relieved”.

Krahmalkov's RḤ III, which he himself marks problematic, compared with Hebrew rêaḥ: only in the title mqm ʾlm mt rḥ ʿštrny, read “rouser of the dead god with the scent of Astronoe” (KAI 44.2; KAI 93). The reading of the title is uncertain.

evidence.locator: p. 442, RḤ III (problematic); p. 308, MQM ʾLM MT RḤ ʿŠTRNY

cognates.gloss: (h-stem) widen, enlarge; (st-stem) be at peace, be safe
cognates.note: Sabaic. The causative hrwḥ is used of enlarging a city's boundary and a plantation (R 2865/1–2; R 4369/2); the st-stem of a camp that “was saved and at peace” (C 334/13). Widening answers to רֶוַח “space” and מְרֻוָּחִים “spacious”; being safe and at peace to רֶוַח beside הַצָּלָה in Est 4:14. Biella's noun rḥ “spirit” occurs only in a Christian inscription's “holy spirit” (C 541/3), which she calls a loan translation, and is not counted here.
Jewish Aramaic of the Targums, rendering רוּחַ of the spirit of God and of the wind (Targ. Gen 1:2; 8:1; 6:17; 45:27; Onq. Num 16:22). Aramaic ח does not show whether ḥ or ḫ stands behind it.

evidence.locator: SEM000375 rwḥ [wind] N: ARM028229 rwḥ [wind] N

cognates.gloss: be wide, be eased, feel relieved; wide space, relief
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the verb “to be wide, extend; to be easy … to feel relieved”, in the Targum of Job 32:20 for Hebrew וְיִרְוַח; the noun “wide space, relief” (Targ. Ps 18:20; Targ. 2Sa 22:20), rendering Hebrew מֶרְחָב “a broad place”.
Jewish Aramaic: the noun and the aphel verb both in the Targum of Gen 27:27, and the verb in Targ. Exo 30:38 and Job 39:25, where the Hebrew has the hiphil of רִיחַ.

evidence.locator: s.v. רֵיחַ ²; s.v. רִיחַ ², Af.

doctrine.statement: The flood destroyed “all flesh in which is the spirit of life”, and “all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life” died, man and beast together (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22). The Preacher says that man and beast “all have one רוּחַ, and man has no advantage over the beast … all go to one place; all are from the dust and all return to the dust” (Ecc 3:19–20). When God takes away their breath they die and return to their dust (Psa 104:29); when a man's breath goes out he returns to his earth, and “in that very day his thoughts perish” (Psa 146:4); the spirit returns to God who gave it (Ecc 12:7), as a loan returns to its owner, and the psalmist calls man “a breath that passes and does not come again” (Psa 78:39). Jesus on the cross and Stephen at his death committed their spirit to God (Luk 23:46, quoting Psa 31:6; Act 7:59). In Ezekiel's valley the slain live again only when breath from the four winds enters them, which Yahweh explains: “I will put my spirit in you and you shall live” (Ezk 37:9–10, 14). From the verses: man's spirit is the breath of life God lends to the dust, the same in man and beast; it is not a conscious self that lives on, for at death the thoughts perish; to commit it to God is to trust him to give life again, and life comes again only when he puts his spirit in the dead at the resurrection.

The spirit of God hovered over the waters at the beginning (Gen 1:2), and “by the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath (רוּחַ) of his mouth” (Psa 33:6; Job 26:13; 33:4). The psalmist asks, “where shall I go from your spirit, or where flee from your presence?” and answers that heaven, the grave and the sea's far end are all within its reach (Psa 139:7–10). Micah is “full of power, of the spirit of Yahweh” (Mic 3:8), and Isaiah sets God against man as spirit against flesh (Isa 31:3). Yahweh took of the spirit that was on Moses and put it on seventy elders (Num 11:17, 25); Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit (2Ki 2:9); Yahweh pours it out like water on the thirsty (Isa 44:3). Isaiah asks who has measured or directed the spirit of Yahweh, and Paul gives the question as “who has known the mind of the Lord?” (Isa 40:13; Rom 11:34). From the verses: the spirit of God is his own breath, mind and power going out from him, by which he creates, sees and reaches everywhere, and works in men; it is spoken of as divided, measured, taken and poured, the language of a power God gives, not of a second person beside him.

Yahweh promises, “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy” (Joel 3:1–2), and on the day of Pentecost Peter says of the apostles' speaking, “this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel” (Act 2:16–18). Isaiah ties the outpouring to the land's renewal: “until the spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field” (Isa 32:15; 44:3). Ezekiel ties it to Israel's final regathering, after Gog's fall: “I will not hide my face from them any more, for I have poured out my spirit on the house of Israel” (Ezk 39:29); and Zechariah: “I will pour on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication, and they will look on me whom they pierced” (Zec 12:10), which John applies to the one pierced on the cross (Jhn 19:37). From the verses: the pouring out of Yahweh's spirit began at Pentecost on the apostles, as Peter says; its full measure on the house of Israel comes when they are gathered to their land and look on the one they pierced, at Christ's return.

The servant of Yahweh is the one on whom he puts his spirit (Isa 42:1), and the anointed one says, “the spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to bring good news to the poor” (Isa 61:1). Jesus read that passage in Nazareth and said, “today this scripture is fulfilled in your ears” (Luk 4:18–21); Matthew says his healing fulfilled Isa 42:1 (Mat 12:17–18). The shoot of Jesse “shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath (רוּחַ) of his lips he shall kill the wicked” (Isa 11:4), and Paul says the Lord Jesus will consume the lawless one “with the spirit of his mouth” at his coming (2Th 2:8). From the verses: Jesus is the Messiah, the anointed, because Yahweh's spirit was put on him; by it he preached and healed at his first coming, and by the same breath of his mouth he will judge at his return.

When the spirit of Yahweh left Saul, “an evil spirit from Yahweh terrified him”, and when David played the lyre Saul was relieved and the evil spirit departed (1Sa 16:14, 23). God “sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously” (Jdg 9:23); Yahweh “put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these your prophets” (1Ki 22:23); he “mixed a spirit of confusion” within Egypt (Isa 19:14) and poured on Jerusalem “a spirit of deep sleep”, which Paul applies to unbelieving Israel (Isa 29:10; Rom 11:8); he would put a spirit in Sennacherib so that he heard a rumour and went home (2Ki 19:7). Zechariah promises that Yahweh will remove “the prophets and the unclean spirit” from the land together (Zec 13:2). From the verses: these spirits are states of mind (fear, enmity, falsehood, confusion, stupor) named by what they do, and scripture says each is from Yahweh, sent as his judgment; they are not beings acting against him, and music could ease the one on Saul.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Leviticus 23 (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ, Lev 23:13, 18); no word of the root occurs in Numbers 10, and רוּחַ itself does not occur in Lev 23. Root key רוח as the database keys it; the Aramaic noun רֵיחַ is keyed ריח (xt.ag.ac) and carries that as its own root. BDB keys and counts: t.bk.ab (Hebrew רוּחַ, 386) and xt.ag.ab (Aramaic רוּחַ, 246) are matched by spelling, so xt.ag.ab counts most Hebrew רוּחַ tokens as well as Daniel's (its true Aramaic uses are Dan 2:35; 4:5, 6, 15; 5:11, 12, 14, 20; 6:4; 7:2, 15); the Aramaic word's use count is far too high. xt.ag.ac likewise counts Hebrew רֵיחַ in Hos 14:7 and Sng 4:10, 11; 7:9 beside Dan 3:27. t.bk.ad (the verb) counts יֶרַח “Jerah” in Gen 10:26 and 1Ch 1:20 (which belong to the name, j.dk.ad) and shares 1Sa 26:19 with it; the real verb tokens are the eleven hiphils. Zero-token cross-references claimed: t.cm.am (רִיחַ) on the verb and xt.aj.ac (Aramaic רֵיחַ) on the Aramaic noun. Root keys t.bk.aa and xt.ag.aa left unclaimed, as other entries leave theirs. The hiphil הֵרִיחַ is taken as a verb of this root (formed from רֵיחַ, which goes with רוּחַ as Arabic rāʾiḥa with rīḥ); some list a separate root ריח. Peshitta: SEDRA root 1744 ROK, lexemes 2972 (verb, 2Co 6:13; 1Ti 5:10), 2973 ROKA (478 tokens), 2974–2976 (ܪܘܚܢܐ “spiritual”, 1Co 2:13–15; 15:44–46; 1Pe 2:5; not entered), 2977 ROKTA (2Co 8:13), 2978 RO;KA (Mat 7:13); root 1759 R;K, lexemes 3015 (verb “smell”: 1Co 12:17, and 2Co 6:11, which is ܪܘܝܚ “enlarged” and belongs to 2972) and 3016 R;KA (Jhn 12:3; 2Co 2:14–16; Eph 5:2; Php 4:18). Syriac lemma pointing follows the SEDRA vocalisation. Payne Smith not consulted. Krahmalkov p. 442 and Biella pp. 481–482 read from the local text layer only (OCR); Segert p. 201 and Fisher pp. 185–186 likewise. Not entered: Ge'ez. Fisher p. 186 gives Tigre and Ge'ez words for spirit, for making a breeze by fanning and for a fan, and Anderson–Moser give Ge'ez rəḥya “be odorous” (GEZ004679), but the OCR is illegible and Dillmann and Leslau were not consulted, so no Ge'ez form is recorded. No Akkadian cognate found (Akkadian uses šāru for wind); Oracc's candidates by consonants are unrelated. Arabic rāḥa “palm of the hand” and Ugaritic rḥ II “hand, palm” (Fisher p. 186) are another word and not entered. Doctrine already written elsewhere and not repeated here: nuach.json “spirit-rests-upon” (Num 11:25; 2Ki 2:15; Isa 11:2) and “acceptable-offering” (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ, Eph 5:2); chayil.json “holy-spirit” (Zec 4:6; Luk 1:35); chadash.json “a-new-heart-and-spirit”; asaph.json “breath-gathered” (Psa 104:29; Job 34:14; Ecc 12:7). Open questions: (1) 1Ki 22:19–23 read as a vision of Yahweh's decision, the “spirit” standing for the false prophecy he sends; (2) Gen 3:8 לְרוּחַ הַיּוֹם left as “breeze of the day”; (3) Lam 3:56 לְרַוְחָתִי “my relief” or “my breathing”; (4) Isa 11:3 הֲרִיחוֹ read as “his smelling”, a sense of discernment; (5) Psa 104:4 kept under “wind” though Heb 1:7 reads πνεύματα.
